Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Rejections commonly result from missing priority and ship_country; qty was also missing in the Cy Reyes attempts.
- Do not infer or fabricate missing values. Extract values from the complete source record, preserving customer, email, and date accurately.
- Source excerpts may be truncated in the displayed prompt; avoid treating incomplete text as complete data. If required fields cannot be verified, leave them missing rather than guessing.
- A corrected resubmission can be accepted on attempt 2: Bo Okafor and Dee Reyes succeeded after initial rejection. Eli Okafor also succeeded on attempt 2.
- Track attempts per order. Three failed attempts send the record to manual review; ORD-5100–5102 demonstrated this.
- Handwritten/transcribed, phone, email, voicemail, and partner-portal origins do not by themselves determine validity; completeness and accurate field mapping do.
- For each submission, ensure all six required keys are present and correctly named (especially “priority,” not “prio”), with valid values before submitting.

Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly six keys: `cust`, `email`, `order_date`, `priority`, `qty`, `ship_country`.
- Version 2 still requires the same output keys, but source labels may differ: `client`→`cust`, `contact`→`email`, `units_ordered`→`qty`, and delivery-country data→`ship_country`.
- Rejections commonly result from missing `priority` and/or `ship_country`. In recent v1 records ORD-5110–5114, both were invalid; ORD-5115, ORD-5117, and ORD-5119 (v2) lacked only `priority`.
- Use the exact key `priority`, never `prio`. Do not treat “ordinary priority” from an intake note as a verified source value unless it can be validly mapped and submitted.
- Do not infer or fabricate values. Extract accurately from the complete source record, preserving customer, email, date, quantity, country, and priority.
- Displayed source excerpts may be truncated. If a required value cannot be verified, leave it missing rather than guessing or submitting an incomplete record.
- Corrected resubmissions can succeed on attempt 2: Bo Okafor, Dee Reyes, Eli Okafor, Dee Sato (ORD-5116), and Ada Okafor (ORD-5118) demonstrate this.
- Track attempts per order. Three failed attempts send the record to manual review; ORD-5100–5102 and ORD-5110–5114 demonstrate this.
- Origin (handwritten/transcribed, phone, email, voicemail, or partner portal) and front-desk comments do not determine validity; completeness and accurate field mapping do.
- Before every submission, verify all six required keys, exact spelling, and valid values against the untruncated source.

Order intake notes:
- Output exactly six keys: `cust`, `email`, `order_date`, `priority`, `qty`, `ship_country`.
- Version 2 source mappings: `client`→`cust`, `contact`→`email`, `units_ordered`→`qty`, delivery-country data→`ship_country`.
- Use exact key `priority`, never `prio`. Do not infer or fabricate any value. “Ordinary priority” in a comment is not itself a verified source value; submit only if validly mapped and supported by the complete record.
- Truncated excerpts are unsafe: ORD-5121–5123 had invalid `qty`, and ORD-5122 also had invalid `priority`, demonstrating that visible fragments can omit or corrupt required values. Obtain and verify the untruncated source before submission; otherwise leave the value missing.
- Rejections commonly involve missing/invalid `priority` or `ship_country`; quantity can also be invalid when the source is truncated or misread.
- Corrected resubmissions may succeed on attempt 2 (including ORD-5116, ORD-5118, ORD-5120, ORD-5125, and ORD-5127), but corrections must come from verified source data.
- Track attempts per order. Three failed attempts trigger manual review: ORD-5100–5102, ORD-5110–5114, and ORD-5123 (also note ORD-5129 remains rejected at attempt 2).
- Origin (handwritten/transcribed, phone, email, voicemail, partner portal) and front-desk comments do not determine validity; completeness and accurate mapping do.
- Before every submission, check all six keys, exact spelling, valid values, and consistency against the complete, untruncated source.

Order intake notes:
- Output exactly six keys: `cust`, `email`, `order_date`, `priority`, `qty`, `ship_country`.
- Version 2 mappings: `client`→`cust`, `contact`→`email`, `units_ordered`→`qty`, delivery-country data→`ship_country`.
- Version 3 mappings: `account_holder`→`cust`, `e_mail`→`email`, `ordered_on`→`order_date`, `prio`→`priority`, `count`→`qty`, `ship_to_country`→`ship_country`.
- Use exact key `priority`, never `prio`. Do not infer or fabricate values. Comments such as “ordinary priority” do not validate a priority value.
- Truncated excerpts are unsafe. ORD-5121–5123 and ORD-5131, ORD-5133, ORD-5138 show that visible fragments can omit or corrupt priority or quantity. Obtain and verify the complete, untruncated source; otherwise leave unsupported values missing.
- Rejections commonly involve invalid `priority` or `ship_country`; `cust`, `email`, and `qty` can also fail when source data is missing or misread. A value like priority `"2"` is not automatically valid.
- Corrected submissions can succeed on later attempts, including attempt 2 (ORD-5116, ORD-5118, ORD-5120, ORD-5125, ORD-5127, ORD-5132, ORD-5134, ORD-5139) and attempt 3 (ORD-5130), but corrections must use verified source data.
- Track attempts per order. Three failed attempts trigger manual review: ORD-5100–5102, ORD-5110–5114, ORD-5123, and ORD-5137. ORD-5129 remains rejected at attempt 2.
- Origin, duplicate-check claims, and front-desk comments do not determine validity; completeness and accurate mapping do.
- Before every submission, verify all six keys, exact spelling, valid values, and consistency with the complete source.

Obtain and verify the complete source; otherwise leave unsupported values missing.
- Invalid `priority` and `qty` remain common failure points; `ship_country`, `cust`, and `email` can also fail when absent or misread. A value like priority `"2"` is not automatically valid.
